what_matters.head: SK Hynix was down about 4.0% and Samsung about 3.2% at 13:05 Seoul time, in Korea's first session since Thursday. The 5.0% and 4.0% falls shown below are too large.
what_matters.detail: Korea was shut on Friday for Hangul Day. The data run took the closed day for missing data and measured both moves from a Yahoo figure (1,699,000 and 264,000 won) instead of Thursday's closes (1,681,000 and 262,000 won). Their five-day moves are right: SK Hynix −11.9%, Samsung −8.2%. In the two US sessions since Seoul's Thursday close, SK Hynix's US-listed shares fell 5.2%. No report gives a cause for this morning's fall.

what_matters.head: Wednesday carries three scheduled releases: the MAS policy statement in the morning, ASML's results at 13:00 SGT and US September consumer prices at 20:30. TSMC reports on Thursday at 14:00.
what_matters.detail: MAS has not announced a time; 08:00 SGT is the calendar's. The companies' forecasts and the options-implied moves are under Earnings.

what_matters.head: Trump said on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an 'energy ceasefire', effective immediately. Neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed it.
what_matters.detail: Oil fell in Asian trading on Monday: Brent crude was 1.8% lower at $102.84 a barrel at 11:14 SGT, and US crude 1.8% lower at $90.22. The ceasefire claim is not in Friday's US prices.

after_data.text: The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday that Amazon is in talks to buy Decart, an AI start-up whose software lets developers move work between different AI chips, in a deal that could be worth about $7 billion. Anthropic had earlier been in talks to buy it for about $6 billion and ended them. Not in Friday's US prices.

latest.tape_note: US stocks rose on Friday, but chip stocks fell again: SOXX, the chip-stock fund, lost 0.7% on the day and 5.0% on the week. Palantir closed at a record (see Movers). The 10-year Treasury yield edged up to 5.24%. Gold rose 1.4%, about its usual daily swing; oil was little changed. The US dollar was flat against the Singapore dollar.
latest.tonight: The US bond market is shut for Columbus Day; stocks trade as usual. No high-impact US release is scheduled. The OCP Global Summit, where the big cloud companies and chip makers discuss data-centre hardware standards, opens in San Jose; its first keynotes start at 07:00 SGT Tuesday.
